MODULE-TO-MODULE ARC: verified by direct read of run-the-first-experiment.md — the lecture is wired at line 35 between 'The far half of the map' and 'Test and learn', matching the maintainer block's placement rationale (line ~30) verbatim; the module's own 'Start here' text does NOT literally echo bullet 1's headline (checked: grep for 'calling tools' / 'LLM in a loop' / 'thing you are sending' against run-the-first-experiment.md returns no match) — the prior audit pass's claim of a verbatim echoing lead-in line does not hold against the current file and has been dropped from this pass's trace rather than carried forward unverified. This does not weaken the arc claim: the module's actual 'Start here' text ('This is the first long one... running without you watching') still hands off cleanly into a lecture whose job is naming the machine behind that long run. BIG IDEA FIDELITY: M4's Big Idea (prep the first long session; the session is how you find out what's missing) is honoured — bullet 4 and the tool-list prompt ground the exact mechanism and surface the exact tool set the send-off will carry. MOOD-DOESN'T-RESOLVE-EARLY: no M5 'learning through contrast' vocabulary present, no packaging recipe taught, no over-resolution of M4's own curious-readiness ahead of the exercise. One recorded, non-blocking wrinkle: bullet 1's headline ('An agent is an LLM calling tools in a loop') foregrounds tool-calling as the loop's defining activity, while the same bullet's third sentence concedes not every iteration calls a tool ('either responds to you or uses tools') — a same-bullet grammar seam that resolves within the slide (bullet 3: the loop runs 'until the agent decides to stop', covering the no-tool-call/respond-only branch) and doesn't threaten the sibling definitional contract with agents-101's what-is-an-agent.md (four-parts list — context, tools, goal, autonomy — unchanged).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Narrow-lens suggestion only: if the same-bullet grammar seam is worth closing, the fix is local to bullet 1's own third sentence, not the headline — name that a tool-call is what USUALLY closes an iteration, with a plain reply as the loop's exit condition, so 'calling tools in a loop' and 'either responds to you or uses tools' read as a rule and its named exception rather than two competing claims about what the loop is for.
